title: Nimbus Strategic Alliance — Deal Acceleration Council
summary: High-level co-sell planning to accelerate three prioritized deals; agreed to run two joint pilots (one hosted, one private), deliver a partner battlecard, and surface security + procurement materials. Discussed routing, pricing collars, exec alignment, and next milestone dates.
action_items: Samira Patel: Share co-sell battlecard + partner pricing spreadsheet by 2026-07-10
Ethan Hughes: Schedule sandbox access and run a 24-hour perf smoke test for Deal A by 2026-07-14
Jian Li / Hector Morales: Provide network diagrams and VPC peering constraints by 2026-07-12
Priya Anand: Add Nimbus contacts to joint success plan doc and create champion map by 2026-07-11
next_steps: Samira to send battlecard and pricing link
Schedule SE-led pilot kickoff (hosted) for Deal A week of 7/13
Schedule private VPC pilot planning call w/ Nimbus infra 7/15
Redwood to share SOC2 + infra security package via secure link
transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-07-08 16:00 UTC — Duration: 53 minutes — Attendees listed above.

00:00 Samira Patel: All right, everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — align the three deals we pre-scored, decide pilots, and list what we need for procurement.
00:15 Olivia Park: Thanks Samira, appreciate it. We want to move the biggest one, Deal A, through sales in the next 6 weeks if possible. we've got exec sponsor locked but need a clearer co-sell plan.
00:30 Marco Ruiz: Yeah one note — our legal team flagged data residency for a few customers, also pricing band concerns.
00:45 Ethan Hughes: Just to call out, from a technical side, the main question is hosted vs private for each use-case. latency sensitivity on Deal A means we probably want a dedicated cluster or private VPC.
01:10 Jian Li: latency is non-negotiable on the real-time routing use-case, we need <80ms p95. what's your experience running that on Redwood hosted versus dedicated?
01:30 Ethan Hughes: In our perf runs, hosted with smart batching and prefix cache hits often sits in the 60–90ms range for short prompts, but variability can spike. Dedicated pools give a tighter SLA but cost more. you trade predictability for unit economics.
02:05 Hector Morales: When you said prefix cache, do you mean KV cache? I think the ops team called it something else in the doc. transcribed earlier as key cache so want to make sure we align.
02:22 Samira Patel: yes KV cache — sometimes mirror text in the docs as key-value cache, the docs are a bit inconsistent, sorry about that. we'll share a clarified glossary.
02:40 Marco Ruiz: ok — second question on co-sell economics: how do we credit the partner in renewal? we need clear margins to show our sales reps.
03:00 Samira Patel: we propose a standard co-sell split for partner-led deals: 70/30 for net-new in the first year, with step-downs on renewals; we can show sample math in the battlecard.
03:20 Olivia Park: good, can you also show an example T-shirt sizing for typical monthly token volumes? our AE needs the quick metric to pitch.
03:35 Samira Patel: yep — we'll include S/M/L usage profiles and rough token cost impacts.
03:50 Ethan Hughes: technical note: for the private trial we recommend starting with a minimal pod sized for 8 concurrent streams and we can autoscale to 32 if metrics look good — that keeps initial cost low.
04:20 Jian Li: what's required from our side for a private deployment — network peering, firewall rules, certs?
04:35 Ethan Hughes: network diagrams, CIDR ranges, allowed outbound ports, and if you want customer-managed KMS we'll need details on HSM or KMS endpoints.
04:55 Hector Morales: okay we can get that. we'll also need a runbook for failover and for cache warmup — it's been a pain historically.
05:15 Ethan Hughes: we'll attach a cache warmup playbook to the pilot runbook.
05:35 Olivia Park: procurement will want SOC2, ISO certs, plus an audit log sample and retention terms. do you have a standard package?
05:50 Samira Patel: yes, we'll share the security pack. note: private customers often sign a stronger DPA and choose longer retention windows; we'll mark that in the battlecard.
06:10 Marco Ruiz: competitor question — ZephyrAI offered a 45% discount if we move two deals within 30 days, how do we counter that?
06:30 Samira Patel: discounts are negotiable within certain bands; instead of competing on pure discount we can offer a bundled pilot credit and a dedicated SE day to accelerate implementation which is often more convincing.
06:50 Olivia Park: can Redwood do an executive briefing with our CEO and the prospective customer execs? that usually helps.
07:05 Samira Patel: yes we can coordinate an exec briefing. recommend we have the sponsor and our CE lead on the call. we'll propose 2 possible dates in the follow-up.
07:25 Jian Li: on the integration side for Deal B (the analytics use-case) the customer needs embeddings at scale; quantization options were mentioned in your docs but some terms were garbled. can you clarify quantization levels and accuracy trade-offs?
07:50 Ethan Hughes: short answer: Q4 and Q5 profiles reduce memory footprint but may affect rare token accuracy; for embeddings we often recommend mixed-precision with a validated eval set. we'll provide model/quantization recommendations per workload in the pilot proposal.
08:25 Hector Morales: is there a way to route cold-class requests to a cheaper model variant automatically? we have cost constraints at scale.
08:40 Ethan Hughes: yes — smart routing policies can route by latency budget or cost tiers; we can set fallback to a lower-cost quantized variant for non-critical paths.
09:05 Marco Ruiz: procurement timeline question: if procurement wants a private deployment do we have a standard handoff?
09:20 Priya Anand: from CSM side we run a 30/60/90 success plan; for private, we add an infra onboarding phase and a 2-week stabilization window.
09:40 Olivia Park: excellent. for Deal C (mid-market upsell) we might do hosted only to keep costs low. which metrics should we watch to decide if we migrate to dedicated later?
10:00 Ethan Hughes: monitor p95 latency, cache hit rate, and token cost per 1k. once p95 breaches the SLO consistently or cost per active session grows past projection, we recommend dedicated.
10:30 Samira Patel: quick recap so we all line up: Deal A — pilot private cluster for latency-sensitive customer; Deal B — hosted pilot focused on embeddings and quantization; Deal C — hosted trial with options to scale. will we agree on that?
10:50 Olivia Park: yes agreed.
11:05 Marco Ruiz: next step on my side is to get legal engaged if we go private. they will need the network diagrams and draft DPA.
11:20 Samira Patel: we'll send the security pack and a draft DPA redline to start.
11:35 Jian Li: timeline check — can we kick off pilot for Deal A on 7/13? that gives us a week to get infra ready.
11:50 Ethan Hughes: 7/13 is tight but doable if Nimbus sends network info by 7/12.
12:10 Hector Morales: we'll target 7/12 for network artifacts.
12:25 Priya Anand: i'll create the joint success plan doc and invite Nimbus contacts; i'll also put milestone owners.
12:40 Samira Patel: thanks — i'll share the battlecard and pricing spreadsheet today and the security pack via secure link.
12:55 Marco Ruiz: good — also please add an example contract clause for co-sell crediting terms.
13:10 Samira Patel: will do.
13:25 Olivia Park: anything else?
13:30 Samira Patel: last note — we should loop in our partnerships legal for one quick sync with Nimbus legal to smooth DPA timelines, i'll propose a time in the follow-up.
13:45 Olivia Park: thanks everyone.
13:50 Meeting end.

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., quantization levels, KV cache named inconsistently). Recorded audio quality medium; some crosstalk between Marco and Olivia at 06:10–06:30.
notes: Shared artifacts referenced: partner battlecard (link to be sent), security pack (SOC2/ISO), sample pricing spreadsheet, pilot runbook
Nimbus to deliver network diagrams and KMS details by 2026-07-12
